html:
The Noongar are the Aboriginal people of the south-west corner of Western Australia, from around Geraldton to Esperance. They call their land Noongar boodja, and have lived there for at least 45,000 years.

They are a bloc of fourteen language groups with closely related speech, among them the Whadjuk of the Perth area, the Ballardong, the Pinjarup, Wardandi and Bibbulman of the forests, the Minang around Albany and the Wudjari of the south coast.

British settlement began at King George Sound in 1826 and at the Swan River colony, now Perth, in 1829. Settlers took the best land, and in 1834 soldiers killed many Pinjarup at the Pinjarra massacre. Later laws controlled where Noongar could live and work. In the mid-2010s they reached a native title settlement with the state. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
